text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- "I appologize to all Bulgarians for the sufferings caused by all politicians in the past seven years," Bulgaria's outgoing President Zhelyu Zhelev said in his New Year's Eve address to the Bulgarian nation.

-- The International Monetary Fund might withdraw its support for Bulgaria and reconsider its proposal for the introduction of a currency board system if the ruling Bulgarian Socialist Party does not radically change its economic policy, a senior official of the main opposition Union of Democratic Forces said.
-- Bulgaria has lifted customs duties on the import of 450,000 tonnes of milliong wheat and 150,000 tonnes of fodder wheat in 1997, trade ministry officials said.

-- Bulgaria's state gas monopolist Bulgargas is expected to discuss with the Russian RAO Gasprom on January 13-14 delivery of six billion cubic metres of Russian gas for Bulgaria in 1997, Bulgargas executive director Petar Sabev said.

-- Industry Minister Lyubomir Dachev said Russian private company Elit had shown serious interest in buying Bulgarian fork-lift truck producer Balkankar and the sale procedure was expected to be finalised by mid-March.

-- Bulgaria and Romania are expected to approach the European Union in January to extend some 7-8 million Ecus for the reconstruction of the bridge over the river Danube, Bulgarian construction ministry officials said
